chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah az-Zuhri who said: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ayyoob, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khath’ami who said: Muhammad ibn Issam narrated to me from Wuhayb ibn Hafs, from Abu Basir who said: Abu Ja'far (or Abu Abdullah - the doubt is from Ibn Issam)

O Abu Muhammad, regarding Al-Qa'im there are two signs: a mole on his head and dandruff on his head, and a mole between his two shoulders, on his left side under his left shoulder, a leaf like the leaf of a myrtle tree.
ai.seo_question: What are the physical signs of Al-Qa'im mentioned in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the physical *alamat* (signs) of Imam al-Mahdi, specifically noting a mole and dandruff (*hazzaz*) on his head and a distinctive mark on his left shoulder. These features serve as tangible identifiers for the Shi'a community during the period of the Minor and Major Occultation, reinforcing the belief in his unique physical lineage and presence. The inclusion of these specific details underscores the scholarly emphasis on verifying the Imam's identity through both textual tradition and observable physical traits.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (5) Abdul Wahid bin Abdullah narrated from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Rabah az-Zuhri from Ahmad bin Ali al-Himyari from al-Hasan bin Ayyoob from Abdul Kareem bin Amr al-Khath’ami from Muhammad bin Issam from Wuhayb bin Hafs that Abu Ja’far al-Baqir (as) (or Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) ) had said:
“Al-Qa’im (as) has two marks; dandruff and a mole on his head and a mole between his two shoulders on the left side. Under the left shoulder there is a mole like the leaf of a myrtle tree.”
